title: Emoji Crowned as ‘Word of the Year’
main_content:
The Oxford Dictionary’s “Word of the Year” is not even a word, it’s an emoji.

Officially called the “Face with Tears of Joy” emoji, it was chosen because it “best reflected the ethos, mood, and preoccupations of 2015,” according to an Oxford Dictionaries blog post.

According to Oxford Dictionaries, “an emoji is a small digital image or icon used to express an idea or emotion in electronic communication.”

The word is Japanese in origin, a combination of the word “e” (picture) and “moji” (letter or character).

Oxford Dictionaries said it partnered with a mobile tech company, SwiftKey, to determine which emoji was used most around the world. In the U.S., the Face with Tears of Joy emoji accounted for 17 percent of all emoji use, up from 9 percent last year.

“Emojis are no longer the preserve of texting teens,” according to the blog post. “Instead, they have been embraced as a nuanced form of expression, and one which can cross language barriers.”

And what of the word emoji? The company said it has been in use since 1997, but that its usage tripled in 2015.

Emojis went mainstream in 1999 when Japanese designer Shigetaka Kurita issued a collection of 180 of them.

Other words that were in contention were “on fleek,” which means very good or stylish, “lumbersexual,” a word used to describe a type of urban hipster who wears a checkered flannel shirt and beard.

questions.question: Why was the “Face with Tears of Joy” emoji chosen as Word of the Year?
options: It was the most frequently used emoji in the U.S. in 2015.
It represented the diverse range of human emotions during 2015.
It best reflected the ethos, mood, and preoccupations of 2015.
It was created by Japanese designer Shigetaka Kurita in 1999.
questions.answer: It best reflected the ethos, mood, and preoccupations of 2015.

questions.question: What is an emoji, according to Oxford Dictionaries?
options: A complex textual symbol used in formal writing.
A small digital image or icon used to express an idea or emotion.
A form of artistic expression exclusive to the digital age.
A type of language that emerged from social media platforms.
questions.answer: A small digital image or icon used to express an idea or emotion.

questions.question: How much has the “Face with Tears of Joy” emoji been used in the U.S., compared with other emojis?
options: It accounted for 9 percent of emoji use in 2014.
It was used less than 17 percent of total emoji use.
It accounted for 17 percent of all emoji use in 2015.
Its usage decreased from 17 percent to 9 percent from 2014 to 2015.
questions.answer: It accounted for 17 percent of all emoji use in 2015.
